core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Fitrah corresponds to the Arabic form فِطرة (Arabic root ف ط ر (f-ṭ-r)). Its core sense is innate nature, original disposition. Fitrah (فِطرة) is the Arabic word for the innate, original human disposition towards God and goodness, from the root ف ط ر (f-ṭ-r) 'to originate, create'. It appears in the Qur'an (30:30, 'the fiṭrah of Allah upon which He created mankind'). It is noted here as a QUR'ANIC WORD; its use as a personal given name is a separate, later naming practice and is not itself Qur'anic. The source gloss 'pure nature, innate disposition' is defensible.
